workEn: The Secret History of the Mongols
title: 元朝秘史 §§100–104
titleEn: The Secret History of the Mongols — §§100–104: The Hiding on Burqan Qaldun
source: Mongγol-un niγuča tobčiyan (The Secret History of the Mongols), §§100–104, in the Ming Chinese-character phonetic transcription, as edited with a romanized reading by Shiratori Kurakichi 白鳥庫吉, 音訳蒙文元朝秘史 (Tokyo, 1943), itself based on the Ye Dehui 葉德輝 printed edition of 1905/1908; text taken from the Japanese Wikisource transcription, archived and verified against it character for character. Shiratori died in 1942, so the edition was public domain in Japan before the URAA date and was never restored in the United States. Section numbering (§) is the standard citation system. Romanization convention: Shiratori's, kept exactly as he prints it (γ, ġ, ṅ, ž, č, and the raised dot of γ̇). Translations are made fresh from the Mongolian, with the Ming interlinear Chinese glosses as the primary crib. No modern translation was consulted. langCode is null: there is no text-to-speech for Middle Mongol.
about: Five sections: the pursuit and the gratitude on the mountain. In §100 Temüjin and his brothers ride up Burqan, while the old woman Qo'aqchin tries to hide Börte-Üjin in a cart and meets the soldiers who have come. In §101 the soldiers break open the cart, take the women, and follow Temüjin's trail toward Burqan. §102 tells how the three Merkid chiefs, who came to avenge Högelün's capture, circle Burqan Qaldun three times without finding him and go home. In §103 Temüjin comes down, strikes his breast, and thanks the mountain, with belt hung on his neck, hat on his hand, nine kneelings to the sun. §104 takes him, Qasar and Belgütei to To'oril Wang Qan, who recalls the sable coat and the old pledge and promises two tümen of his own and two of Jamuqa's against the Merkid.
draftNote: The Mongol readings follow Shiratori throughout; the English is a first drafting.

sentences.t: Temüžin aqa-nar deġü-ner morilažu erte böġed Burqan žüg γarba.

morph.gloss: Temüjin, a boy's name (personal name) [人名]
horse; -la- makes it a verb, 'to mount' [馬上着]
early, in former times (adjective, adverb) [疾早]
to be; ending -ġed, 'being so, then, at once' (analysis uncertain) [便]
Burqan, the holy mountain (mountain name) [山名]
to go out, to go up [上了]

sentences.l: Temüžin, elder-brothers, younger-brothers, having-mounted, early, then Burqan toward went-up.
sentences.i: Temüjin and his elder and younger brothers mounted early and went up toward Burqan.
sentences.n: The subject is Temüjin and his brothers; aqa-nar and deġü-ner are aqa and deġü with the plural -nar / -ner (Ming 每), so 'the elder brothers and the younger brothers'. morilažu (上馬着) is mori 'horse' made a verb by -la- and closed by the converb -žu, 'having mounted'. Ming 疾早 glosses erte 'early'; böġed (便) I take as bü- 'be' with -ġed, 'then, at once', but that analysis is uncertain. žüg (處) is 'place, direction', so Burqan žüg is 'toward Burqan'; γarba is γar- 'go out, go up' plus the past -ba. The full stop is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: Γoγ̇aγčin emegen Börte-Üžin-i niγ̇usu keġen.

morph.gloss: Qo'aqchin, a woman's name (personal name) [婦人名]
Börte-Üjin, a woman's name (one two-part name) [(婦人)名 行]
to hide (stem inferred from the Ming 要藏 'want to hide') [要藏]
optative: let me ... (compare ögsü); with keġen, 'intending to' (Ming 要藏 'want to hide'; analysis uncertain)
converb that closes a quotation or thought: saying

sentences.l: Γoγ̇aγčin the-old-woman, Börte-Üžin (acc.), to-hide, saying.
sentences.i: The old woman Qo'aqchin, wishing to hide Börte-Üjin,
sentences.n: Börte-Üžin-i is one two-part name with the accusative -i, so Börte-Üjin is the thing hidden. niγ̇usu (要藏) is niγu- 'hide' with an ending -su that the Ming reads as 'wanting to'. I take it to be the optative -su of ögsü and morilasu in §104 ('let me ...'), so that niγ̇usu keġen is 'saying "let me hide"', that is, 'intending to hide'; the analysis is not certain. keġen is keġe- 'say' with the converb -n, which closes a thought or a quotation: here 'saying (to herself), intending'. The sentence runs on into the next unit.

sentences.t: nigen qaraγ̇utai tergen-dür unuγ̇ulžu

morph.gloss: to ride, to sit in [敎坐着]

sentences.l: One black-having cart-in, having-made-sit,
sentences.i: she seated her in a black cart,
sentences.n: qaraγ̇utai is qara 'black' with -tai 'having' (the back-vowel twin of -tu / -tü), so 'black-having', that is black; the Ming 黑有的 shows the possessive. tergen-dür is tergen 'cart' plus the dative-locative -dür, Ming 裏 'in'. unuγ̇ulžu (敎坐着) is unu- 'ride, sit in', the causative -γ̇ul- 'make ...', and the converb -žu: 'having made her sit'. The object, Börte-Üjin, is carried over from the last unit.

sentences.t: böġere alaγ hüker kölžü

morph.gloss: to yoke, to harness (stem inferred from the Ming 駕着) [駕着]

sentences.l: Waist-mottled ox, having-yoked,
sentences.i: and yoked a waist-mottled ox to it,
sentences.n: böġere alaγ hüker: hüker is 'ox' (牛), alaγ is 'mottled, dappled' (花) and böġere is 'waist, loins' (腰), so the ox was mottled at the waist. I keep 'waist-mottled' and do not try for a tidier ox. kölžü (駕着) I take as köl- 'to yoke, harness' with the converb -žü; the stem is inferred from the Ming and is uncertain.

sentences.t: Teṅgeli γoroqan öġede ködölžü aisun büküi-dür

morph.gloss: Teṅgeli, a river name (the same letters write 'axle' in §101) [河名]
to move (stem inferred from the Ming 動着) [動着]

sentences.l: Teṅgeli brook against-the-current, having-moved, coming being-when,
sentences.i: and as she was coming along, moving up against the Teṅgeli brook,
sentences.n: Teṅgeli (騰格里) is here marked 河名 'river name', and γoroqan (小河) is 'small stream', so 'the Teṅgeli brook'; the same Han letters write teṅgeli 'cart-axle' in the next section. Whether this brook is the Tüṅgelig stream of §§5 and 28 (there written 統格黎克, different letters) is not said. öġede (逆着) is 'against the current, up'; ködölžü is ködöl- 'move' plus -žu (stem inferred from the Ming 動着). aisun (來) I read as aisu- 'come' with an ending -n, converb or participle, which is uncertain. büküi-dür is bü- 'be', the participle -küi and the dative-locative -dür, Ming 有的時 'when being, while'.

sentences.t: horubaru-da üdürge-jin büküi-dür

morph.gloss: half-dark, the dim time before day (Ming 尙昏時 'still dark') [尙昏時 行]
near daybreak (Ming 盡將明; analysis uncertain) [盡將明]

sentences.l: Half-dark-in, near-daybreak being-when,
sentences.i: In the half-dark, when day was close to breaking,
sentences.n: horubaru-da is horubaru 'half-dark, the dim time' (Ming 尙昏時 'while still dark'; here before daybreak, not the evening dusk) with the dative-locative -da; üdürge-jin (盡將明) 'near daybreak' with the genitive -jin is uncertain in its analysis. büküi-dür repeats the 'when being' of the last unit; the Ming here writes 有敵時 'when there was an enemy', which seems to run ahead to the next clause, and I translate only the time.

sentences.t: esergünēče čerig haran qataražu hergižü kürčü irežü"

morph.gloss: ablative: from (long vowel from front-vowel stem)
to urge on, to gallop (Ming 點 'prod'; uncertain) [點着]
to circle, to wheel round (stem inferred from the Ming 旋着) [旋着]

sentences.l: From-the-front, soldier people, having-urged-on, having-circled, having-arrived, having-come.
sentences.i: soldiers came riding hard from the front, wheeling about until they arrived.
sentences.n: esergünēče is esergü 'facing, against' with the ablative -ēče (Ming 迎自 'from in front'). čerig is 'soldier, army' and haran 'people, persons' (Ming 人 'persons'), so 'soldier people', troops. The four converbs are a chain: qataražu (點着, qatara- 'urge on, gallop'; the Ming 點 'prod' is uncertain), hergižü (旋着, 'circling'; stem herg- inferred), kürčü (kür- 'reach') and irežü (ire- 'come'). I have shortened the chain in English to a reader's sentence.

sentences.t: jaγ̇un küġün či" keġen hasaγba.

morph.gloss: to ask (the h- is Shiratori's spelling) [問了]

sentences.l: What man you, saying, asked.
sentences.i: "What man are you?" they asked.
sentences.n: A plain question and its frame: jaγ̇un 'what', küġün 'man', či 'you', closed by keġen 'saying'. hasaγba is the verb 'ask' with the past -ba (the h- is Shiratori's spelling of the stem). The questioners are the soldiers and the person asked is the old woman.

sentences.t: Γoγ̇aγčin emegen ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Qo'aqchin, a woman's name (personal name) [婦人名]

sentences.l: Γoγ̇aγčin the-old-woman, saying:
sentences.i: The old woman Qo'aqchin answered:
sentences.n: ügülerün is ügüle- 'speak' with the converb -rün, 'saying' (the quotation marker used throughout this text).

sentences.t: "Bi Temüžin-ü-ġei bi.

morph.gloss: Temüjin, a boy's name (personal name) [人名 的]
is, exists (verb; perhaps a short form of bü-) [有]

sentences.l: I Temüžin-ü-ġei am.
sentences.i: "I belong to Temüjin.
sentences.n: Temüžin-ü-ġei is Temüžin with the genitive -ü and an ending -ġei that the Ming glosses 的 'of'; I take it as 'one belonging to Temüjin', but the formation is uncertain (the glossary has -ġei elsewhere as a verb ending). The final bi is the verb 'is, exists' (有), so 'I am Temüjin's' with no further word for 'people' written.

sentences.t: Jeke ger-tür qoni kirγara ireleġe.

morph.gloss: to shear (stem inferred from the Ming 剃) [剃]

sentences.l: Great home-at sheep to-shear came.
sentences.i: I have come to the great house to shear sheep.
sentences.n: Jeke is 'great, big'; ger-tür is ger 'home' plus the dative-locative -tür. Whether Jeke ger is a name ('the Great House') or only 'a big house' the text does not say. qoni is 'sheep'. kirγara (剃) is kirγa- 'shear' with an ending -ra that I read as 'in order to', a purpose; the ending is uncertain. ireleġe (來了) is ire- 'come' plus the past -leġe, 'had come'.

sentences.t: Ger-tür(i)-jen qarižu aiši" keġebi.

morph.gloss: tent, home, house (noun) [家 自的行]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (the bracketed i is Shiratori's)
to turn back, to return [囘著︀]
present ending 'am, is ...-ing' (Ming 有; analysis uncertain)

sentences.l: Own-home-to, having-turned-back, I-am-coming, said.
sentences.i: Returning to my own home, I am on my way," she said.
sentences.n: Ger-tür(i)-jen is ger plus the dative-locative -tür and the reflexive-possessive -(i)jen, 'to one's own home'; the bracketed i is Shiratori's. qarižu is qari- 'turn back, return' with -žu (Ming 囘着). aiši (來有) I read as ai- 'come' with a present ending -ši, 'I am coming'; the ending is not otherwise known to me and is uncertain. keġebi is keġe- 'say' with the past -bi.

sentences.t: Tendēče ügülerün:

morph.gloss: ablative: from (long vowel from tende plus -eče)

sentences.l: From-there, saying:
sentences.i: Then they said:
sentences.n: Tendēče is tende 'there' with the ablative -ēče, 'from there': 'thereupon'. The speakers are the soldiers.

sentences.t: "Temüžin ger-tür bijü-ü;

morph.gloss: Temüjin, a boy's name (personal name) [人名]
to be; present bijü, 'there is' [有麽]

sentences.l: Temüžin home-at is-he?
sentences.i: "Is Temüjin at home?
sentences.n: bijü is the present 'there is' (bü- 'be'); the following -ü (Ming 麽) is the question particle, the same -ü as in ese-ü later in this part. The semicolon is Shiratori's.

sentences.t: ger kežige bijü" keġebi.

morph.gloss: how far (Ming 幾遠; form uncertain) [幾遠]

sentences.l: Home how-far is, said.
sentences.i: How far off is his home?" they said.
sentences.n: kežige (幾遠) is 'how far'; the form is not otherwise known to me. ger here is simply 'home'; the Ming 家 does not say whose, and I supply 'his' from the question before. bijü again 'there is'.

sentences.t: Γoγ̇aγčin emegen ügülerün:

morph.gloss: Qo'aqchin, a woman's name (personal name) [(婦人)名]

sentences.l: Γoγ̇aγčin the-old-woman, saying:
sentences.i: The old woman Qo'aqchin said:
sentences.n: Same formula as above.

sentences.t: "Ger či oira bijü.

morph.gloss: particle 'as for, if' (Ming 呵; not the pronoun 'you'; uncertain) [呵]

sentences.l: Home, as-for, near is.
sentences.i: "The house is near.
sentences.n: či here is Ming 呵, a mark of 'as for, if' (a topic or conditional particle), and not the pronoun 'you' that či is elsewhere in this part; the same spelling is doing two jobs, and I follow the Ming. oira is 'near, close'.

sentences.t: Temüžin-i büküi-ji ügei ese uqabi.

morph.gloss: Temüjin, a boy's name (personal name) [人名 行]
accusative after a vowel: marks the object

sentences.l: Temüžin (acc.), being (acc.), without, not-yet knew.
sentences.i: Whether Temüjin is there or not, I did not know.
sentences.n: Temüžin-i is the name with the accusative -i and büküi-ji is the participle büküi 'being' with the accusative -ji, so 'Temüjin, his being' is the object of 'know'; ügei is 'without, not', and 'being, not-being' is the way Mongol says 'whether he is there or not'. ese is the negative of the past ('not yet'), and uqabi is uqa- 'know, understand' with the past -bi. So: 'I did not know Temüjin's being-or-not-being'.

sentences.t: Qoināča bosuγ̇ad irebi bi" keġebi.

morph.gloss: to rise, to get up [起了]

sentences.l: Afterward, having-risen, came I, said.
sentences.i: I got up afterward and came," she said.
sentences.n: Qoināča is qoina 'behind, after' with the ablative -ča, 'afterward, from behind'. bosuγ̇ad is bos- 'rise' with the converb -uγ̇ad; irebi is ire- 'come' with the past -bi. The closing bi is 'I' (Ming 我), standing last for emphasis, and keġebi 'said' closes the quotation. The speech is hers throughout: she is telling the soldiers she knows nothing and has only just got up and come.

sentences.t: Tede čeriġüd tedüi qataraba.

morph.gloss: to urge on, to gallop [點着去了]

sentences.l: Those soldiers, so, urged-on-went.
sentences.i: The soldiers rode on at once.
sentences.n: Tede is 'those' (plural of tere) and čeriġüd 'soldiers' (čerig plus the plural -d); tedüi (那般) is 'so, thereupon' as a sentence adverb. qataraba is qatara- 'urge on, gallop' plus the past -ba; the Ming 點着去了 adds 'went off'. They gallop on, leaving the women behind.

sentences.t: Γoγ̇aγčin emegen böġere alaγ hüker(i)-jen deledüġed

morph.gloss: Qo'aqchin, a woman's name (personal name) [(婦人)名]
reflexive-possessive: one's own (the bracketed i is Shiratori's)
to strike (stem inferred from the Ming 打了) [打了着]

sentences.l: Γoγ̇aγčin the-old-woman, waist-mottled ox-her-own, having-struck,
sentences.i: The old woman Qo'aqchin struck her waist-mottled ox,
sentences.n: hüker(i)-jen is hüker 'ox' with the reflexive-possessive -(i)jen (the Ming 自的行 marks 'her own' and the object). deledüġed is deledü- 'strike' (a stem inferred from the Ming 打了) with the converb -ġed, 'having struck'. The next unit says what she did it for.

sentences.t: öterlen neġükü bolun tergen-ü teṅgeli quγus odba.

morph.gloss: to move, to set off [起行]
to break (stem uncertain; Ming 折) [折]

sentences.l: Quickly, to-set-off when-being, the-cart's axle broke went.
sentences.i: to start off quickly, and the axle of the cart broke.
sentences.n: öterlen is öter 'quickly' with the adverbial -len. neġükü is neġü- 'move, set off' (Ming 起行) with the participle -kü, and bolun is bol- 'become, be' with the converb -un, Ming 做呵 'when doing'; neġükü bolun is 'when setting off, on starting'. teṅgeli (車軸) 'cart-axle' is written with the same Han letters as the river Teṅgeli. quγus odba (折 去了) is 'broke and went', a way of saying 'snapped': quγus is a form I cannot analyse (perhaps quγu- 'break'), and od- 'go' with -ba.

sentences.t: Teṅgeli-ben quγuraγdažu jabuγad(i)-jar hoi-dur güjižü oroja keġeldün

morph.gloss: cart-axle (Ming 車軸) [車軸 自的行]

words.reading: 中忽中忽舌剌(黑)荅周 quγuraγdažu
迓步中合的-牙舌兒 jabuγad(i)-jar

morph.gloss: to walk, to go on foot [步行着]
instrumental: by, on (the Ming 步行着 'on foot' as a whole; analysis uncertain)
hortative, first person plural: let us

sentences.l: Axle-her-own, having-been-broken, on-foot into-the-wood having-run, let-us-enter, saying-to-one-another,
sentences.i: With the axle broken, they ran on foot into the wood, saying to one another, "Let us go in,"
sentences.n: Teṅgeli-ben is the axle with the reflexive-possessive -ben, 'her own axle'. quγuraγdažu is quγura- (a stem near quγu- 'break') plus the passive -γda- and the converb -žu, Ming 被折着 'having been broken'. jabuγad(i)-jar (步行着): jabu- 'walk' with the converb -γad, and a token -(i)jar that I read as an instrumental, 'by', so 'on foot'; the formation is uncertain. hoi-dur is hoi 'wood' plus -dur. güjižü is güji- 'run'. oroja is oro- 'enter' plus -ja, the hortative 'let us' (Ming 咱). keġeldün is keġe- 'say' plus the reciprocal -ldü- and the converb -n: 'saying to one another'. The 'they' are Qo'aqchin and the woman she was hiding.

sentences.t: büküi-dür daruča müd čeriġüd Belgütei-jin eke-ji sundulaγ̇uldužu

morph.gloss: at once, immediately (Ming 隨卽) [隨卽]
they (third-person plural; Ming 他每) [他每]
Belgütei, a man's name, a younger brother of Chinggis (personal name) [人名 的]
accusative after a vowel: marks the object
to lay across, to double up (stem uncertain; Ming 疊騎) [敎疊騎着]

sentences.l: Being-when, at-once, those soldiers, Belgütei's mother (acc.), having-made-ride-double,
sentences.i: While they were speaking, the soldiers came back at once with Belgütei's mother, set on a horse doubled up,
sentences.n: büküi-dür 'when it was so'. daruča (隨卽) is 'immediately, forthwith'. müd (他每) is 'they' (the plural of a third-person form), standing with čeriġüd. Belgütei-jin eke-ji is Belgütei with the genitive -jin, eke 'mother' and the accusative -ji. sundulaγ̇uldužu is a causative (-γ̇ul-) converb with -žu: Ming 敎疊騎着 'having made ride one upon the other'; I do not know the stem (sundula- may be 'lay across') and 'doubled up' is only the Ming's picture. Nothing before this says the soldiers had Belgütei's mother; they are returning with her, and the sentence goes on into the next unit.

sentences.t: qojar köd in-ü čerbegelžeġülžü qataražu kürčü ireġed

morph.gloss: two (follows the pair it counts) [兩箇]
foot, leg (plural köd; Ming 腳每) [腳(每)]
his, her, its (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]

words.reading: 扯舌兒別格勒者︀溫勒周 čerbegelžeġülžü

glyphs.s: 扯舌兒別格勒者︀溫勒周

morph.gloss: to hang down, to dangle (stem uncertain; Ming 垂着) [垂着]
to urge on, to gallop [點着]

sentences.l: Two legs her, having-made-dangle, having-urged-on, having-arrived, came.
sentences.i: her two legs hanging down, riding hard until they arrived.
sentences.n: qojar köd in-ü: qojar 'two', köd (腳每) 'feet, legs' (köl 'foot' with a plural), in-ü the third-person genitive 'his, her' set after its noun. čerbegelžeġülžü (垂着 'hanging') I analyse as čerbegel- 'dangle' with -že-, an extension I cannot name, the causative -ġül- and the converb -žü: 'having made hang down'; the analysis is uncertain. The next three converbs are the same chain as in §100: qataražu, kürčü, and ireġed (ire- 'come' with -ġed).

sentences.t: "ene tergen dotora jaγ̇un teġežü amu" keġebe.
sentences.l: This cart inside what having-loaded is, said.
sentences.i: "What is loaded in this cart?" they asked.
sentences.n: ene 'this', tergen 'cart', dotora 'inside'; jaγ̇un 'what'. teġežü (載着) is teġe- 'load' plus -žu, and amu (有) is 'is' (a-, the verb 'to be', with a present ending). The speakers are the soldiers.

sentences.t: Γoγ̇aγčin emegen ügülerün: "Uṅγasun teġežü amu" keġebi.

morph.gloss: Qo'aqchin, a woman's name (personal name) [(婦人)名]

sentences.l: Γoγ̇aγčin the-old-woman, saying: Wool having-loaded is, said.
sentences.i: The old woman Qo'aqchin answered, "It is loaded with wool."
sentences.n: uṅγasun (毛) is 'hair, wool' (the word is used for wool and hair alike). The answer repeats the soldiers' verb, 'loaded is'.

sentences.t: Tede čeriġüd-ün aqa-nar in-ü ügülerün:

morph.gloss: his, her, its, their (third-person genitive, placed after its noun) [他的]

sentences.l: Those soldiers' elder-brothers, theirs, saying:
sentences.i: The elders among those soldiers said:
sentences.n: aqa-nar (兄每) is 'elder brothers', here the senior men of the band; čeriġüd-ün is 'of the soldiers' (the plural -d plus the genitive -ün). in-ü 'theirs' stands after the noun it belongs to, so I take 'the soldiers' elder brothers' as 'their seniors'; the doubled possessive is awkward and I choose the smoother English.

sentences.t: "Deġü-ner köġüd(i)-jen baγ̇užu üžedkün" keġebe.

morph.gloss: reflexive-possessive: one's own (the bracketed i is Shiratori's)
to come down, to dismount [下着]

sentences.l: Younger-brothers, lads-own (acc.), having-descended, look, said.
sentences.i: "Younger brothers, my lads, get down and look!" he said.
sentences.n: Deġü-ner 'younger brothers' and köġüd(i)-jen (兒每自的行) 'sons, one's own' are a call to the junior men: köġüd (köġün 'son' with -d) is 'sons' and so 'lads' of the band, -(i)jen 'my own' referring to the speaker, and the accusative marking is only a loose mark of address. baγ̇užu is baγu- 'come down, dismount' plus -žu; üžedkün is üže- 'see' with an imperative-plural ending -dkün that the glossary already marks uncertain. The reading of köġüd(i)-jen as 'my lads' is a guess from the sense; the form itself means 'one's own sons'.

sentences.n: qaγ̇alγatai is qaγ̇alγa 'gate, door' with -tai 'having', so 'the cart that has a door', and tergen-ü qaγ̇alγa is 'the cart's door'. abqui-luγ̇a is ab- 'take' with a participle -qui and -luγ̇a, which in the glossary is 'together with, as soon as'; the analysis is tentative, and 'the moment they opened' is a reading of the Ming 取了, 'took (off)'. The brothers are the men just called in the last unit.

sentences.i: Following behind Temüjin, they circled Burqan Qaldun three times but could not catch him.
sentences.n: Burqan-Qaldun-(n)i is the mountain name with the accusative -(n)i; γurbanta is γurban 'three' plus the dative-locative -ta, 'three times' (the Ming 三次 'thrice' is the only evidence). qučiγ̇ulžu is 'having made circle, having circled' (Ming 繞着), with the causative -γ̇ul-. erüsün (得) I read as a verb 'obtain, get' with -sün, and jadaba as jada- 'be unable' plus -ba; together 'were unable to get'. What they could not get is Temüjin; that is my reading from the sense (the Mongol has no object). It has no subject yet either: 'they' are the Merkid, named a few units on.

sentences.i: If they dodged this way and that, there was mud to sink in, and it was hard going.
sentences.n: ein tein (這般 那般) is 'thus and so', 'this way and that'. bulžiγ̇asu is bulžiγ- 'dodge' with the conditional -su (Ming 呵 'if'), 'if one dodges'. umubu (陷) and šibar (泥 'mud') I read as 'sinking, mud'; the exact form of umubu is uncertain. berke is 'hard, difficult'. So: 'if one dodges this way and that, sinking mud, hard'; the English keeps the 'if' and supplies 'they' and 'there was' to join the words.

Čiledü-dāča is the man's name with an ablative -dāča 'from' (the long vowel is Shiratori's). buližu is buli- 'snatch, seize' with -žu. abtalaγ̇ai is ab- 'take', the passive -ta- (-da-) and an ending -laγ̇ai that the Ming 被要子 renders 'was taken'; the ending is uncertain. sentences.n: edöġe 'now', tere 'that', ösül 'grievance, enmity' (Ming 讐). ösen is the paired word, 'requital' or 'to requite' (Ming 報 'repay'); in the glossary the pair ösül ösün is 'enmity', and here the pair reads 'avenge the grievance' with ösen as its verb; I cannot analyse the ending. iregsed is ire- 'come' with the past participle -gsen in its plural, 'those who have come', and ažuγ̇u 'were'. I keep the speech in quotation marks, but the Mongol has no marker for the change; the sense runs on from the last unit.

sentences.n: Höġelün-(n)ü is the name with the genitive; hači (讎) is 'enmity, a feud, vengeance'. aburan is abura- 'repay, requite' (報) with the converb -n. emes-i is eme 'woman' with a plural -s and the accusative -i (Ming 婦人每行). an-u (他的) is 'their', the back-vowel partner of in-ü. abuba is ab- 'take' with -ba. sentences.n: Hači-jan is hači 'vengeance' with the reflexive-possessive -(i)jan, 'our own feud', Ming 自的行 (the token is spelled -jan, back-vowel). aburaba is abura- 'repay' plus -ba; bida is 'we' (inclusive, Ming 咱). The next two words are one verb split over a line: keġel- (共說) and dužu (着) are keġe- 'say' with the reciprocal -ldu-, written keġel-|dužu, and the converb -žu: 'having said to one another'. Burqan-Qaldun-(n)ača is the mountain with the ablative; geid-tür(i)-jen is geid (家裏每 'homes', apparently a plural of ger) with -tür and the reflexive -(i)jen, 'to their own homes'. ažiraba (囘去了) is a verb 'go back' with -ba; I do not know the stem ažira-, and 'went back' is from the Ming.

sentences.n: Three names in a row, then γurban-i, γurban 'three' with the accusative -i, 'the three (as object)': the object of the verbs that follow. Merkid-ün is the people with the genitive -ün; qoināča 'from behind'. The Mongol never says 'sent'; it is the sense of the object with the causative daγaγ̇ulžu below, which I read as 'made follow'.

sentences.t: "Γoγ̇aγčin eke-ji solanγa bolžu sonosqu-jin tula ünen bolžu üžekü-jin tula

sentences.l: Γoγ̇aγčin mother (acc.), weasel having-become, because-of-hearing, ermine having-become, because-of-seeing,
sentences.i: "For the sake of hearing Mother Qo'aqchin I became a weasel; for the sake of seeing her I became an ermine;
sentences.n: Γoγ̇aγčin eke-ji is 'mother Qo'aqchin' with the accusative -ji (Ming 行). An accusative is the case of an object, so I read her as the object of the two participles that follow, 'for the sake of hearing Mother Qo'aqchin ... for the sake of seeing her'; a plain address ('Mother Qo'aqchin!') would not take the accusative. The reading is uncertain, and the Ming does not say why he hears and sees her. The speaker is Temüjin, and the subject 'I' is understood. solanγa (黃鼠狼) is 'weasel' and ünen (銀鼠) 'ermine' (literally 'silver mouse'); bolžu is bol- 'become' with -žu. sonosqu-jin tula and üžekü-jin tula are the participles 'hearing' (sonos-) and 'seeing' (üže-) with the genitive -jin and the postposition tula 'because of, for the sake of' (Ming 上頭 'on account of'): 'for the sake of hearing', 'for the sake of seeing'.

sentences.l: Whole body-my-own, hiding,

sentences.n: naran (日處) 'at the sun', jesünte is jesün 'nine' with the dative-locative -te, 'nine times' (Ming 九遍). sögödčü (跪着) is sögö- 'kneel' (stem inferred) with -dčü. sačuli (灑奠) is a sprinkled offering, a libation, and öčiġüli (禱祝) a prayer; I take both as nouns in -li, and ögbe is ög- 'give' with -be: 'gave a libation, gave a prayer'. sentences.n: Three names, then γurban 'three'. Kereid-ün is the people name with the genitive -ün, 'of the Kereid'. Toγ̇oril, Waṅ-Qan-dur: Waṅ is Chinese 'prince' and Qan the Mongol 'ruler', and -dur is the dative-locative, 'to Wang Qan'. The verb 'went' is odču, two units on.

sentences.i: who was then in the Black Forest on the Tula river, and said:
sentences.n: Tuγ̇ula müren-(n)ü: 'of the river Tuγ̇ula' (müren 'river' with the genitive). Qara tün-(n)e is qara 'black' and tün 'forest, wood' with the dative -(n)e, 'at the Black Forest' (Ming 黑 林行). I take 'Black Forest' as a name; the Ming only marks 林 'wood'. büküi-dür 'when being (there)', odču is od- 'go' with -ču. The 'being' belongs to Wang Qan, and the 'going' to the three men, which is why I give them the relative clause.

sentences.n: Γurban Merkid-te: the dative -te, which with the passive abdaba (below) names the doer, 'by the three Merkid'. genen (不想) is 'unexpectedly' (the Ming 'not thinking'), a form I know only from here. büküi-dur 'when it was so' (Ming 有的時分). irežü, 'having come'. eme köġü-ben (婦人 兒子自的行) is 'woman, son, one's own'; eme and köġü are a pair, 'woman and son', with no number marked; 'wife and children' is my loose English for the pair. daγ̇uližu is daγ̇uli- 'plunder' (the glossary: 'analysis uncertain', Ming 擄) with -žu. abdaba is ab- 'take' with the passive -da- and -ba, 'was taken'. The speaker is Temüjin.

morph.gloss: khan, ruler, sovereign (title, the short form beside qaγan) [皇帝]

sentences.l: Khan father my, woman, son-own, having-rescued, let-give, saying, we-came, we, said.
sentences.i: We have come saying, 'Khan, my father, rescue my wife and children and give them to me,'" he said.
sentences.n: Qān ečige min-u: 'Khan, father mine' (Temüjin addresses To'oril as father, because of the old pledge with his own father that To'oril recalls below). min-u 'my' set after its noun. eme köġü-ben as above; aburažu is abura- 'rescue, save' (Ming 救; elsewhere 'repay') with -žu, and ögtügei is ög- 'give' with the third-person optative -tügei, 'let him give' (Ming 與者). irebe is ire- 'come' with -be, and the closing ba (俺) is 'we' (exclusive: we, not you), against bida 'we, you and I'. The plea is a quotation inside Temüjin's longer speech (keġen 'saying'); the closing ba" ends that longer speech and keġebe 'said' is its frame, so the Mongol is 'saying: Khan, my father, ..., we came'. I keep min-u as 'my' and add no 'lord'.

sentences.t: Buluγan daqu na-da abčirarun ečige-jin čaγ-un anda keġeldügsen

sentences.l: Sable fur-coat to-me when-bringing, father's time-in sworn-friend that-have-said-to-one-another,
sentences.i: When you brought me the sable coat, [you said], 'You who swore brotherhood in the father's time,
sentences.n: buluγan daqu is 'sable coat' (貂鼠 襖子). na-da is bi's stem na- with -da, 'to me'. abčirarun is ab- 'take' and čira-, 'bring' (abčira-), with the time converb -run: 'when (you) brought'. ečige-jin čaγ-un is 'in the father's time' (the genitive -jin, then čaγ 'time' with -un, Ming 時裏). anda is 'sworn friend, pledged brother'. keġeldügsen is keġe- 'say' with the reciprocal -ldü- and the participle -gsen, 'that have mutually said'. The words ečige-jin čaγ-un anda keġeldügsen name no person: 'the one who in the father's time mutually declared anda'. They match what Temüjin said in §96 ('you swore brotherhood with my father; you are like a father to me'), so I give them as his words, 'you who swore brotherhood in the father's time', and mark the reading as uncertain. The next unit continues them.

sentences.n: ečige metü: 'like a father' (metü 'like, as', a postposition). bijü-že is bü- 'be' and the assertion particle -že, 'there is indeed'; keġen 'saying' closes the quoted words; who says them is not written (bi is named only in the next unit). They are Temüjin's words in §96, so I write 'you said'; a converb normally shares the subject of its main verb, which would make them Wang Qan's own words, so this is uncertain. emüšgegdeġesü (被穿了呵) is emüs- 'wear' with the passive -gde- and the conditional -ġesü, 'if (I) was clothed (in it)'. I read it as 'having been made to wear it', that is, when the coat was put on him. The grammar is hard and the sense is the Ming's: the conditional gives a time ('when'). Compare emüsgeg in §96 (the first-meeting gift, Ming 上見), perhaps from the same stem emüs-: the coat was that gift.

sentences.l: Black sable-coat's in-return parted people (acc.) your, having-united, give, saying.
sentences.i: In return for the black sable coat I will bring together your people, who have parted from you, and give them,' I said.
sentences.n: The same pattern as above, with the coat now qara 'black' and the people qaγačaγsan, qaγača- 'part from, separate' with the past participle -γsan (Ming 離了的). qamtudγaldužu (相收合着) is qamtu- 'together' (stem inferred) with -dγal-, -du- and -žu, 'having brought together'; I cannot divide it with confidence. ögsü 'I will give'. keġen closes.

sentences.t: čegerei-jin čeġeži-dür atuγai; bököre(i)-jin bögše-dür atuγai

morph.gloss: chest cavity (Ming 腔子) [腔子 的]
diaphragm, breast (uncertain; Ming 胸膈) [胸膈 裏]
optative, third person: let it ..., let him ...

sentences.l: Breast-cavity's diaphragm-in let-it-stay; kidney's tip-in let-it-stay.
sentences.i: Let it stay in the diaphragm of the chest; let it stay in the tip of the kidney.
sentences.n: A saying: čegerei-jin čeġeži-dür is 'in the diaphragm of the chest-cavity' (čegerei 'chest cavity', Ming 腔子; čeġeži 'diaphragm', Ming 胸膈, uncertain, with -dür), and bökörei-jin bögše-dür is 'at the tip of the kidney' (Ming 腰子, 尖兒). atuγai is a- 'be, remain' with the third-person optative -tuγai: 'let it stay'. The sense is 'keep it in mind, keep it close'; the Ming does not say so, and I leave it as the picture. The same words stand in §96, rendered there 'in the tip of the kidney, in the diaphragm of the chest'; whose body is meant is not said.

sentences.t: ese-ü keġeleġe bi.
sentences.l: Not-yet said I.
sentences.i: Did I not say it?
sentences.n: ese-ü is 'did not ...?'; keġeleġe is keġe- 'say' with -leġe, the past 'had said'; bi closes the clause as 'I'. The Ming reads 不曾(麽) 說來, 'did I not say?'.

sentences.t: Edöġe tere üge-dür(i)-jen kürün

morph.gloss: reflexive-possessive: one's own (the bracketed i is Shiratori's)

sentences.l: Now that word-my-own, reaching,
sentences.i: Now, in keeping with those words,
sentences.n: üge-dür(i)-jen is üge 'word' with -dür and -(i)jen, 'to one's own word'. kürün (到) is kür- 'reach' with the converb -n: 'reaching, according to'. So 'now, in accordance with my own word'.

sentences.t: buluγan daqu-jin qariγ̇u bügüde Merkid-i büreltele

morph.gloss: answer, reply, return (noun; Ming 囘 'in return') [囘奉]
to be destroyed (stem inferred from the Ming 毀滅) [直至毀滅]

sentences.l: Sable-coat's in-return, all Merkid (acc.), until-destroyed,
sentences.i: in return for the sable coat, I will wipe out the Merkid, all of them,
sentences.n: bügüde (都) is 'all'; Merkid-i with the accusative. büreltele (直至毀滅) is bürel- 'be destroyed' (the stem is inferred from the Ming) with -tele, 'until'; so 'until they are destroyed'. The Mongol has no verb 'wipe out' here; I take the next unit to supply the main verb.

sentences.t: Börte-Üžin-i čin-u aburažu ögsü bi.

morph.gloss: Börte-Üjin, a woman's name (one two-part name) [婦人名 行]
to rescue, to save (Ming 救; elsewhere 'repay') [救着]

sentences.l: Börte-Üžin (acc.) your, having-rescued, give, I.
sentences.i: and rescue your Börte-Üjin and give her back to you.
sentences.n: Börte-Üžin-i is the name with the accusative -i. čin-u 'your'. aburažu 'having rescued' (the same verb as in Temüjin's plea above), ögsü 'I will give', bi 'I'. The closing quotation mark is not here; it comes at the end of the speech.

sentences.t: qara buluγan daqu-jin qariγ̇u Qamuγ Merkid-i qaltačižu qatun Börte-ji čin-u qariγ̇ulžu abčiraja bida.

morph.gloss: answer, reply, return (noun; Ming 囘 'in return') [囘奉]
to break, to smash (stem inferred from the Ming 破) [破着]
lady, queen, wife of a khan (noun) [娘子]
Börte (short for Börte-Üjin; a woman's name) [婦人名 行]
accusative after a vowel: marks the object
to turn back, to return [囘着]

sentences.l: Black sable-coat's in-return, all Merkid (acc.), having-broken, lady Börte (acc.) your, having-made-return, let-us-bring, we.
sentences.i: In return for the black sable coat we will break the whole Merkid people and bring your lady Börte back to you.
sentences.n: Qamuγ Merkid-i is 'all the Merkid' (qamuγ 'all, the whole', Ming 普). qaltačižu (破着) is qaltači- 'break, smash' (the Ming 破) with -žu. qatun Börte-ji: 'lady Börte' (qatun 'lady'; Börte with the accusative -ji, a short form of Börte-Üjin). qariγ̇ulžu is qari- 'return' with the causative -γ̇ul- and -žu, 'having caused to return, having brought back'. abčiraja is abčira- 'bring' with -ja, the hortative 'let us' (Ming 咱), and bida 'we (you and I)'; Wang Qan now speaks of a joint act with Temüjin, 'let us bring'. The change from 'I' to 'we' is in the Mongol.

sentences.t: Či Žamuqa deġü-de kelen kižü ile;

morph.gloss: Jamuqa, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
to send (as in ilerün, ilebe; the Ming 救去 'rescue, go' does not say so; uncertain) [救去]

sentences.l: You Žamuqa younger-brother-to word having-made, send;
sentences.i: You send word to the younger brother Jamuqa;
sentences.n: Či 'you', Žamuqa deġü-de 'to Jamuqa the younger brother' (deġü 'younger brother' with -de), kelen kižü 'making word' (kelen 'word, speech', kižü ki- 'do, make' with -žü), so 'send word'. ile (救去 in the Ming) I take as ile- 'send' in the imperative; the Ming 救去 does not read as 'send', (it reads 'rescue, go'); the glossary has ile- 'send' (ilerün, ilebe) beside ile 'openly', and I follow 'send' from the sense. Uncertain. The Mongol writes no 'my' or 'your' with deġü, so the English keeps 'the younger brother Jamuqa' in this and the next units.

sentences.t: Žamuqa deġü Qorqonaγ-Žubur-a bi že.

morph.gloss: Jamuqa, a man's name (personal name) [人名]

morph.gloss: Qorqonaq-Jubur, a place name (Ming 地名) [地名(裏)]
is, exists (verb; perhaps a short form of bü-) [有]

sentences.l: Žamuqa younger-brother Qorqonaγ-Žubur-at is, indeed.
sentences.i: The younger brother Jamuqa is at Qorqonaq-Jubur.
sentences.n: Qorqonaγ-Žubur-a is the place name (地名) with the dative -a; bi is the verb 'is' (Ming 有), and že the particle 'indeed'. The place is named without a gloss. Wang Qan tells Temüjin where Jamuqa is.

sentences.t: Bi endēče qojar tümed morilasu;

morph.gloss: makes a verb: to make into, to ...

sentences.l: I from-here two tümen will-mount;
sentences.i: From here I will ride out with two tümen;
sentences.n: endēče is ene 'here' with the long-vowel ablative -ēče. qojar tümed is 'two tümen' (tümen 'ten thousand', here with the plural -d, Ming 萬每), so a force of 20,000. morilasu is mori 'horse' made a verb with -la- and given the optative -su: 'let me mount, I will ride'. Shiratori's semicolon is kept.

sentences.t: baraγ̇un γar bolun, Žamuqa deġü qojar tümed bolžu žeġün γar bolun morilatuγai.

morph.gloss: right (hand or side; adjective; Ming 右) [右]
Jamuqa, a man's name (personal name) [人名]
left (hand or side; adjective; Ming 左) [左]
makes a verb: to make into, to ...

sentences.l: Right hand being, Žamuqa younger-brother two tümen having-become, left hand being, let-him-mount.
sentences.i: I will be the right hand, and let the younger brother Jamuqa ride with two tümen as the left.
sentences.n: baraγ̇un γar bolun (右 手 做) is 'right hand, being' (bol- 'become' with the converb -un): 'to be the right hand'. Žamuqa deġü qojar tümed bolžu: 'Jamuqa, with two tümen, becoming'. žeġün γar bolun is 'to be the left hand'. morilatuγai is mori 'horse', -la-, and the third-person optative -tuγai: 'let him ride'. The two wings of a Mongol army are the right and the left hand.

sentences.t: bidan-u bolžaγ̇an Žamuqa-dāča boltuγai" keġebe

morph.gloss: we, us (inclusive: you and I; first-person plural pronoun, Ming 咱) [咱的]
to appoint, to agree on a meeting (stem inferred; Ming 約會) [約會]
Jamuqa, a man's name (personal name) [人名 處]

sentences.l: Our appointment Žamuqa-from let-it-be, said.
sentences.i: Let our meeting be fixed by Jamuqa," he said.
sentences.n: bidan-u is the genitive of bida 'we', 'our'. bolžaγ̇an (約會) is an appointment, a fixed meeting, the stem bolža- (from bol- 'become') with an ending I cannot name. Žamuqa-dāča is the name with a long-vowel ablative 'from Jamuqa', which here I read as 'from Jamuqa's side, by Jamuqa'. boltuγai is bol- 'be' with the optative -tuγai, 'let it be'. keġebe closes Wang Qan's speech.
